jurisdictionName: Bexar County / City of San Antonio ETJ, TX
sourceDocument: City of San Antonio Unified Development Code, Article V (Development Standards), Sec. 35-506 'Transportation', Table 506-3 (Street Design Standards); Supp. No. 22. Road/grade values verified 2026-08-28 against the provided UDC PDF. Parking-lot and driveway-approach slopes are NOT specified in the UDC (see notes) and are left unset pending the COSA Storm Water Design Criteria Manual and TxDOT driveway criteria.
_comment_scope: Values below are transcribed from the COSA UDC only. Bexar County unincorporated development in the SA ETJ follows these subdivision/street standards. City limits permit a slightly higher local-street grade (12%) than the ETJ (10%); the ETJ value is used here as the conservative Bexar County default.
_comment_standardParking: The UDC does NOT specify a parking-lot SURFACE slope max/min. That is governed by the COSA Storm Water / paving design criteria, not the UDC. Left null so the tool's conservative engineering default (5% max / 1% min) applies. Populate once the drainage design manual value is confirmed.

driveAisleOrRoad.notes: UDC Table 506-3 & Sec 35-506(d)(3): local street max grade 10% in ETJ (12% in city limits); collectors 7%, arterials 5%, alleys 10%. Min grade 0.5% (0.4% permitted with concrete curb & gutter). SEPARATE road cross-slope standard: min 2% / max 4% (Sec 35-506(d)(3)A) - not yet representable in this single-axis schema; enforce in review.

generalLot.notes: Basis: UDC Sec 35-673(c)(2) requires graded (riverbank) slopes not to exceed 4:1 (25%) for erosion stability; grade changes over 10 vertical feet must be benched/terraced. Detention basin slopes must not exceed 3:1 (33.3%) (parkland/detention standard). No general-lot grading cap is stated in the UDC; 25% (4:1) adopted as the conservative stable-slope max. Min 1% for positive drainage (engineering default, not UDC-specified).

_comment_drivewayApproach: The UDC does NOT specify a driveway-approach grade. Driveway approaches in the SA/Bexar area follow TxDOT 'Access Management' / driveway criteria and COSA transportation standards, not the UDC. Left null pending that source.
_comment_ada: Accessible-surface limits are NOT taken from the UDC. They come from the federal 2010 ADA Standards (Sec 402/502) and the Texas Accessibility Standards (TAS, TDLR-enforced), which the tool already hardcodes as non-overridable floors. Only populate an accessible* field here to make a limit STRICTER than ADA; a looser value is rejected at load.
_comment_ratios: H:V ratios. UDC references: 4:1 max stable graded slope (Sec 35-673), 3:1 max detention-basin slope. RetainingWallTrigger is an engineering-practice value (2:1), NOT a UDC-specified threshold - confirm against the COSA grading/retaining-wall standards before relying on it.
